field.description: Standard work item field name to evaluate (e.g. 'tags', 'priority', 'state', 'title').

operator.description: Comparison operator. equals/not-equals: exact match. contains/not-contains: substring or array membership. gt/lt/gte/lte: numeric comparison.

value.description: Value to compare against. Can be a string, number, or boolean.

customField.description: Azure DevOps custom field reference in 'Namespace.FieldName' format (e.g. 'Custom.ClientTier').

operator.description: Comparison operator. equals/not-equals: exact match. contains/not-contains: substring or array membership. gt/lt/gte/lte: numeric comparison.

value.description: Value to compare against. Can be a string, number, or boolean.

all.description: Sub-conditions that must all match (logical AND).

any.description: Sub-conditions where at least one must match (logical OR).

formatVersion.description: Which edition of the Atomize schema this file follows. Currently "1.0"; omit it to mean "1.0". Not the template's own revision: that's version.

version.description: The author's own revision of this file, e.g. '1.2' or '2026-10'. Free text: Atomize shows it but never interprets it.

name.description: Unique display name for this template.

description.description: What this template is for and when to use it.

author.description: Author or team that owns this template.

tags.description: Tags for template discovery in the catalog.

created.description: Deprecated: nothing in Atomize reads or maintains it. Version control records when the file was created.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

lastModified.description: Deprecated: nothing in Atomize reads or maintains it, so it goes stale. Version control records changes.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

team.description: Azure DevOps team name. Limits story selection to stories owned by this team.

workItemTypes.description: Work item types to include (e.g. ['User Story', 'Bug']). With savedQuery, declares which types the query returns: it doesn't filter, but tells Atomize which fields to look up and validate.

statesExclude.description: Story states to exclude from selection.

statesWereEver.description: Include stories that were ever in any of these states.

include.description: Include stories that have at least one of these tags.

exclude.description: Exclude stories that have any of these tags.

tags.description: Tag-based filter — include or exclude stories by tag.

areaPaths.description: Area paths to filter by. Use '@TeamAreas' to match all areas owned by the configured team.

areaPathsUnder.description: Include stories in these area paths and all sub-paths.

iterations.description: Iterations to filter by. Use '@CurrentIteration' for the active sprint.

iterationsUnder.description: Include stories in these iterations and all sub-iterations.

assignedTo.description: Assignee filter. Accepts email addresses or '@Me' for the authenticated user.

changedAfter.description: Include stories changed after this date. ISO 8601 date or date macro (e.g. '@Today-7').

createdAfter.description: Include stories created after this date. ISO 8601 date or date macro.

priority.description: Priority range filter for story selection.

excludeIfHasTasks.description: If true, skips stories that already have child tasks.

path.description: Path to the saved query in Azure DevOps (e.g. 'My Queries/Sprint Stories').

x-atomize-rules: Set exactly one of id or path.

savedQuery.description: Reference an existing Azure DevOps saved query to select stories.

filter.description: Criteria used to select which stories this template applies to.

id.description: Unique identifier for this task within the template. Referenced by 'dependsOn'.
x-atomize-rules: Non-empty task IDs must be unique within the file.

title.description: Task title — shown as the work item title in Azure DevOps.

description.description: Additional details or notes for this task.

estimationPercent.description: Percentage of the parent story's estimate assigned to this task (0–100). Requires estimation.strategy = 'percentage'.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. Applied when this condition matches.

percent.description: Estimation percentage used when this condition matches (0–100).

estimationPercentCondition.description: Conditional estimation rules evaluated in order. The first matching condition's percent is used.

estimationFixed.description: Fixed point value for this task, independent of the parent story's estimate.

estimationFormula.description: Deprecated: formulas were never evaluated and give the task a Task Estimate of 0. Use estimationPercent or estimationFixed.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

tags.description: Tags applied to the generated task.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. If it does not match, this task is skipped.
x-atomize-rules: Offline Validation of a Template warns when this condition references custom fields; Online Validation is needed to verify that those fields exist on the platform.

dependsOn.description: IDs of tasks this task depends on. Atomize creates predecessor dependency links between these tasks.
x-atomize-rules: In a Resolved Template, dependencies must reference existing task IDs and must not form a cycle, including a dependency on the task itself.
A task with repeat set cannot have a non-empty dependsOn, and another task cannot depend on it, even when repeat is 1.
A task with dependencies should have its own id; validation reports a warning when it does not.

repeat.description: Number of identical Tasks to generate from this definition (default 1). Each copy's title gets its position, e.g. 'Review (2)'. Cannot be combined with dependsOn.
x-atomize-rules: When repeat is set, dependsOn must be absent or empty and other tasks cannot depend on this task, even when repeat is 1.
In a Resolved Template, repeat must not exceed validation.maxRepeat (20 by default). A Mixin defers this cap to the composing Template.

assignTo.description: Email address or alias to assign this task to.

priority.description: Priority value for the generated task.

activity.description: Azure DevOps activity type for this task (e.g. 'Development', 'Testing', 'Design').

acceptanceCriteria.description: Deprecated: acceptance criteria are never written to the generated task. Put them in description instead.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

acceptanceCriteriaAsChecklist.description: Deprecated: acceptance criteria are never written to the generated task, so this setting has no effect.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.
Every key must be a platform field reference in Namespace.FieldName format, such as Custom.ClientTier.
customFields.description: Azure DevOps custom fields to set on the task. Keys must be in 'Namespace.FieldName' format (e.g. 'Custom.ClientTier').

tasks.description: Task definitions that will be generated from this template.

taskType.description: Work Item type generated Tasks are created as, in the platform's own vocabulary (e.g. 'Task', 'Sub-task'). Omit to use the platform default.

strategy.description: Estimation strategy. 'percentage' distributes the parent story's estimate across tasks proportionally.

source.description: Story field that supplies the Story Estimate, as a platform field reference name (e.g. 'Custom.TShirtSize'). Replaces the platform's default fields, with no fallback. Omit to use the platform default.

factor.description: Multiplier from the Story's unit to the Task's unit, e.g. 4 when 1 point = 4 hours.

x-atomize-rules: The conversion table must contain at least one entry.
table.description: Story Estimate value to Task-unit amount, matched exactly, e.g. { XS: 1, S: 2, M: 4, L: 5 } or { 1: 2, 2: 4, 3: 8 } for scales that aren't linear.

multipliers.description: Also accept a number followed by a table key, e.g. '0.3XL' = 0.3 × XL. Exact keys still win. Requires a table with non-numeric keys.
x-atomize-rules: When multipliers is true, conversion.table must be set and at least one table key must be non-numeric.

conversion.description: Translates the Story Estimate into the Task's unit before it is split across tasks. Set exactly one of factor or table; omit for one-to-one.
x-atomize-rules: Set exactly one of factor or table.

targetFields.description: Task fields that receive the Task Estimate, as platform field reference names. Replaces the platform's default estimate fields entirely; values are written exactly as calculated.

normalize.description: What to do when the generated tasks' percentages don't add up to 100%. 'auto' (default) scales totals below 100% up and leaves totals above 100% as written unless you choose otherwise at generate time; 'always' scales to 100% in both directions; 'never' uses the percentages exactly as written, so a skipped task's share stays unallocated.

rounding.description: Rounding mode applied to calculated task estimates: 'nearest', 'up', 'down', or 'none'.

minimumTaskEstimate.description: Minimum Task Estimate any single task can receive after rounding, in the Task's unit.

minimumTaskPoints.description: Deprecated: use minimumTaskEstimate. Still honoured when minimumTaskEstimate is absent.
x-atomize-rules: minimumTaskEstimate takes precedence when both minimum fields are set. Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

ifParentHasNoEstimation.description: Behaviour when the Story Estimate is missing or cannot be converted. 'warn' (default) creates the tasks with blank estimates and reports a warning, 'skip' creates no tasks for the Story, 'use-default' uses defaultParentEstimation instead.

defaultParentEstimation.description: Story Estimate used when the real one is missing or cannot be converted and ifParentHasNoEstimation is 'use-default', in the Story's unit (e.g. 'M' or 5). Goes through the same conversion as a real Story Estimate.
x-atomize-rules: When ifParentHasNoEstimation is use-default and this value is set, it must be convertible: numeric without a table, or a matching conversion.table key (including enabled multipliers).

estimation.description: Global estimation configuration for all tasks in this template.

mode.description: 'strict' treats blocking validation warnings as errors; 'lenient' allows warnings. Non-blocking advisories remain warnings in both modes.

totalEstimationMustBe.description: Sum of all non-conditional task percentages must equal this value exactly. It may exceed 100 when tasks span roles.

totalEstimationRange.description: Sum of all non-conditional task percentages must fall within this range; bounds may exceed 100 when tasks span roles.

minTasks.description: Minimum number of tasks the template must define.

maxTasks.description: Maximum number of tasks the template may define.

maxRepeat.description: Highest 'repeat' any task in this template may use (default 20). Raise it for a template that genuinely needs more copies.
x-atomize-rules: This cap applies to every task definition in the Resolved Template, including tasks contributed by Mixins.

min.description: Minimum allowed estimation percentage for a single task.

max.description: Maximum allowed estimation percentage for a single task.

taskEstimationRange.description: Inclusive bounds for each final task percentage after normalization, including percentage rounding. Fixed estimates are excluded.
x-atomize-rules: min must be less than or equal to max.

Checked after normalization and its percentage rounding, per repeated copy. With normalize: never, supplied percentages are used unchanged. Fixed estimates are excluded. Story-dependent conditions and percentage overrides are checked during preview and generation, once the active allocation is known. Task Estimate rounding in hours or points does not change this percentage constraint.

id.description: Required task ID. Checked first; falls back to title match if absent.

requiredTasks.description: Tasks that must be present in the template, matched by title or id.
x-atomize-rules: Each required entry must match an existing task by its supplied id or its title. Both comparisons are case-insensitive; a title match is accepted even if the supplied id does not match.
